keyboard.action: On an item or its handle: pick the item up. Announce its position ("item 2 of 5").
While picked up in a vertical list: move the item one position later and announce the new position.
While picked up in a vertical list: move the item one position earlier.
While picked up in a horizontal list or grid: move the item one position later.
While picked up in a horizontal list or grid: move the item one position earlier.
While picked up: move the item to the first position.
While picked up: move the item to the last position.
While picked up: drop the item at its current position and announce the result.
While picked up: cancel, return the item to where it started and announce it.
While picked up: drop (or cancel, by configuration) and move on; a picked-up item must not survive loss of focus.
On a draggable item: start a keyboard drag.
During a keyboard drag: move to the next valid drop target (between items, on an item, or another collection).
During a keyboard drag: move to the previous valid drop target.
During a keyboard drag: drop on the focused target.

focus.entry: The collection keeps its own strategy; the picked-up item keeps DOM focus while it moves.
focus.exit: Drop, cancel, or focus leaving the collection.
focus.restore: After drop or cancel, focus is on the moved item at its final position.
focus.note: Two models exist. Move mode keeps focus on the item and moves it with arrows (the common sortable-list model). Drop-target mode (React Aria, read from source) keeps the item in place and cycles focus through drop targets with Tab, which also covers dragging between collections.

variants: explicit move buttons (move up, move down) as the non-drag alternative

rtlDecisions.question: While an item of a horizontal list is picked up for keyboard reordering in RTL, which arrow moves it later in the order?

libraries.behaviour: Keyboard drag does not use arrows: Enter starts, Tab cycles drop targets, Enter drops, Escape cancels. Drop-position maths treats a horizontal list in RTL as reversed.

rtlDecisions.reason: The picked-up item must travel in the direction of the arrow; in RTL the later positions are to the left.

data.notes: WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.7 requires a non-dragging alternative for pointer users as well; move buttons or a "move to" menu satisfy it. Move-mode bindings are convention (as in dnd-kit and similar libraries, whose source was not read) and need review. RTL: in a horizontal list the later positions are to the left, so ArrowLeft moves the item later (decision reorder-arrows, ours; no library evidence for arrow-based horizontal moves). Vertical moves are unaffected. In a tree, the arrow that indents (nests under the previous sibling) is the one that points to inline-end. Announcements carry positions as numbers and need Arabic plural forms.
